new_scholarship.deadline: Financial aid application deadlines for the 2027-2028 academic year: November 1, 2026 (Posse Scholar), November 15, 2026 (Early Decision I), December 1, 2026 (QuestBridge), January 3, 2027 (Early Decision II), February 1, 2027 (Regular Decision), March 1, 2027 (Fall 2027 Transfer) and November 1, 2027 (Spring 2028 Transfer)
new_scholarship.application_period: 2027-2028 academic year aid cycle: the CSS Profile and FAFSA deadlines are November 1, 2026 (Posse Scholar), November 15, 2026 (Early Decision I), December 1, 2026 (QuestBridge), January 3, 2027 (Early Decision II), February 1, 2027 (Regular Decision), March 1, 2027 (Fall 2027 Transfer) and November 1, 2027 (Spring 2028 Transfer). The admissions application itself is due November 2 for Early Decision I and January 4 for Early Decision II and Regular Decision, so the aid deadline is the binding one for this award.
new_scholarship.application_method: Not a separate scholarship application. Aid is awarded automatically within the admission process: the applicant submits the Common Application, Coalition Application, or QuestBridge Application and files Middlebury's financial aid application, the CSS Profile being required for every prospective undergraduate applying for aid and mandatory for international students, with the FAFSA additionally required for US citizens and eligible noncitizens. Aid must be applied for by the published financial aid deadline; the College states it is need aware in the admission of international students and that applicants seeking financial assistance must apply for aid when they apply for admission. The final offer is issued in early summer after Middlebury verifies the financial aid application of every undergraduate who enrolls, and is viewed in the Middlebury Financial Aid Portal.
new_scholarship.description: Middlebury College publishes no single named international scholarship; the funding it publishes for international undergraduates is need-based institutional financial aid, and the College states that if you are an undergraduate student admitted to Middlebury, it will meet your full demonstrated financial need, with almost all of its aid being institutional grants and scholarships that do not have to be repaid. Published figures are institutional rather than award-specific: $80M institutional aid awarded, 50% of students receiving aid, 100% calculated need met, a $66K average grant, and 100% need-based aid. For international applicants the College states it is need aware, so assistance must be requested when applying for admission, the CSS Profile is required for all prospective undergraduates filing for aid and is the only accepted international route, and the College does not accept the ISFAA or a paper CSS Profile. Aid includes all books and supplies, higher-need students also qualify for student health insurance and a new laptop, and the College states it is tuition-free for families with annual incomes up to $175,000.
new_scholarship.best_fit: International first-year or transfer applicants to Middlebury who can document financial need through the CSS Profile and, for international parents, non-US tax forms or employer earning statements, and who can meet the published financial aid deadline for their application round.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Aid is awarded to admitted Middlebury undergraduates on demonstrated financial need only; the College publishes '100% Calculated Need Met', '100% Need-Based Aid' and a $66K average grant across all recipients, and states it meets the full demonstrated financial need of admitted undergraduates. Every prospective undergraduate applying for aid must file the CSS Profile (Middlebury College school code 3526), and international students must submit it electronically because the College does not accept the ISFAA or a paper copy; international applicants also submit parent non-US tax forms or employer earning statements translated into English, plus a parent non-filing statement where applicable, through the College Board IDOC service. The FAFSA (school code 003691) is required for US citizens and eligible noncitizens. About 15% of Middlebury students carry international passports or were raised outside the United States. No per-annum amount, currency or period is published for this aid, and no separate merit scholarship for international applicants was confirmed on the official pages read.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: Selection is need-based rather than merit-based. The College publishes '100% Calculated Need Met', '$66K AVERAGE GRANT' and '100% Need-Based Aid', and states that it will meet the full demonstrated financial need of admitted undergraduates. Eligibility for the aid is determined by the CSS Profile, which the College states is used to determine eligibility for need-based Middlebury College funding, and every enrolled undergraduate's financial aid application is verified before the final offer is issued in early summer. For international applicants the College is need aware, and the published aid deadlines are binding because assistance must be requested when applying for admission. No published weighting between academic merit and financial need was found on the pages read.
new_scholarship.notes: Middlebury publishes no named international scholarship on the pages read, so this record captures the College's need-based institutional financial aid, which is the only international undergraduate funding mechanism verified on Middlebury's own pages. The record name follows the assignment target wording but describes need-based aid, not a merit award. No amount, currency or period is published for this aid, so those fields are null; the published $66K average grant is an all-recipient institutional average and the $175,000 figure is an income threshold, not an award amount. Two cost questions remain unanswered by the official pages: which components of the cost of attendance the international need calculation includes, and whether travel to Vermont is covered, so living_cost_coverage and travel_coverage are null and fully_funded is false. The CSS Profile carries a College Board fee and Middlebury states it relies on the College Board's waiver determination and does not provide fee waivers.

programme_detail_official.description: Middlebury College publishes no single named international scholarship; the funding it publishes for international undergraduates is need-based institutional financial aid. The College states that if you are an undergraduate student admitted to Middlebury it will meet your full demonstrated financial need, and that almost all of its financial aid is institutional grants and scholarships that do not have to be repaid. Its published figures are institutional rather than award-specific: $80M institutional aid awarded, 50% of students receiving financial aid, 100% calculated need met, a $66K average grant, and 100% need-based aid. For international applicants the College is need aware, so assistance must be requested when applying for admission and no later than the published deadlines, the CSS Profile is required for every prospective undergraduate applying for aid and must be submitted electronically for international students, and supporting parent tax forms or employer earning statements translated into English go through the College Board IDOC service. The College verifies the financial aid application of every undergraduate who enrolls and issues final offers in early summer. Aid includes all books and supplies, and higher-need students also qualify for student health insurance and a new laptop.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Full demonstrated financial need as calculated by the College for admitted undergraduates, covering tuition and the components included in the College's need calculation, with all books and supplies included and student health insurance and a laptop for higher-need students; travel is not listed as covered and no per-annum amount is published.

alerts.message: For Early Decision I the application is due November 2, 2026 but the financial aid application is due November 15, 2026, and for Regular Decision the application is due January 4, 2027 with the aid application due February 1, 2027, so the later aid date is the one that governs funding.

The College states that international applicants must apply for financial assistance when they apply for admission, no later than the deadlines on its website, so a late request loses aid consideration for that cycle.

There is a fee to submit the CSS Profile. Middlebury relies on the College Board's determination of eligibility for waivers and states it does not provide fee waivers, so check College Board waiver eligibility before submitting.
Middlebury does not accept the ISFAA or a paper copy of the CSS Profile as alternatives to the electronic CSS Profile.
The $175,000 tuition-free threshold the College publishes is an income threshold for families, not a scholarship amount you can apply for separately.

The College verifies the financial aid application of every undergraduate who enrolls and issues final offers in early summer, in the Middlebury Financial Aid Portal, after the file review is complete.

submission_workflow: Submit the Common Application, Coalition Application, or QuestBridge Application for your chosen round

Invite at least two teachers to submit recommendations
Ask the school counselor to send the school report, counselor recommendation, and transcript directly to the Admissions Office
Upload senior-year or midyear grades as the round requires
Submit an English proficiency score if your native language is not English or your schooling was not entirely in English
Monitor the Slate admissions portal for additional document requests, which the College states may follow once review begins
Review and accept or decline the final offer in the Middlebury Financial Aid Portal when it appears in early summer

research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: The funding is undergraduate aid. The Student Financial Services page addressed is Apply for Aid for First-Year and Transfer Students and states that if you are an undergraduate student admitted to Middlebury it will meet your full demonstrated financial need; the admissions Application Instructions and Deadlines page covers first-year and transfer admission to the bachelor's degree and refers to 'a full-time degree-seeking program' with a minimum of 18 units of credit; the Apply page profiles the Class of 2030 entering the undergraduate college; and the financial aid page refers to 50% of Middlebury students receiving aid and to 'Higher need students' in undergraduate terms.
research_notes.award_choice: Middlebury publishes one need-based mechanism rather than a named international scholarship, and its own pages state '100% Need-Based Aid' and '100% Calculated Need Met', with the Student Financial Services page stating that the CSS Profile 'is used to determine your eligibility for need-based Middlebury College funding'. That need-based institutional aid is therefore the single best-documented funding for international undergraduates and is what this record captures, named 'Middlebury College Financial Aid for International Students'. No separate need-blind merit award, and no named endowed international fund, was found on the pages read within the four-fetch budget, so no merit variant is recorded; the merit picture for international applicants remains unverified rather than confirmed absent.
research_notes.international_need_aid_finding: Verified on Middlebury's own pages that international students DO receive need-based aid and that Middlebury is need aware, not need blind, for them. The admissions page states: 'We are need aware in our admission of international students. If you are seeking financial assistance, you must apply for aid when you apply for admission, no later than the deadlines indicated on our website.' The Student Financial Services page adds that the College will meet the full demonstrated financial need of admitted undergraduates, that the CSS Profile is required of every prospective undergraduate applying for aid, and that Middlebury does not accept the ISFAA or a paper copy of the CSS Profile. Aid is therefore automatic on admission in the sense that no separate scholarship application exists, but it is not automatic in the sense that it must be requested by the published financial aid deadline.
research_notes.fetch_budget: Four fetches on middlebury.edu were used: one that resolved to the Apply page, the financial aid hub, the admissions Application Instructions and Deadlines page, and the Office of Student Financial Services apply-for-aid page for first-year and transfer students. The logo URL was additionally probed with a direct HTTP request for status, content type, byte length and fill colours, which is a byte probe rather than a page read.
